currentContext.business: Founded in 1981, Ecoplast manufactures high-quality multilayer coextruded polyethylene and co-polymer films, having played a major role in developing India's flexible packaging industry as a supplier of lamination grade films. In view of poor margins and fierce competition in the commodity lamination business, the Company transitioned into a purely value-added product business, and since 2024 has focused on specialty films, adhesive films, surface protection films and the export market. Following the NCLT-sanctioned merger of sister concern Kunal Plastics Private Limited, one of the largest manufacturers of PE bags in India, all business and operating entities within the group now stand consolidated under Ecoplast Limited.

currentContext.expansion: Since 2024 the Company has committed more than Rs 75 crores towards a series of greenfield and brownfield expansions, described as significantly reinforcing its manufacturing capabilities for the years ahead. The combined annual production capacity will go up from ~9000 MTPA (2024) to ~13600 MTPA after full expansion is commissioned. The final tranche of machinery is currently being installed and is on track for commissioning by the end of the second quarter of FY 2026-27. Together with the completion of the amalgamation of sister concern Kunal Plastics Private Limited (one of the largest manufacturers of PE bags in India) - approved by the Board on December 14, 2024, sanctioned by the NCLT on May 14, 2026 with an appointed date of April 1, 2025 and effective from May 28, 2026 - this expanded capacity places the Company on a meaningfully broadened product portfolio spanning surface protection films, specialty films and PE bags, with benefits expected to start flowing through progressively over the course of FY 2026-27. Separately, the wholly owned subsidiary Synergy Films Private Limited has been shut down since 7 December 2019 as economically unviable, and the Board approved its winding up / closure on May 22, 2024 subject to regulatory approvals.

risks.risk: US export tariffs and trade-policy uncertainty
risks.note: Management lists Export Tariffs as a threat: with the USA a key export market, additional tariffs on Indian products pose a meaningful risk to export realizations and order flow. This already bit in FY26 - increased trade tariffs announced by the USA on India, and the resulting uncertainty, affected export orders and realizations during the year, forcing the Company to develop new customers in other export markets.

risks.risk: Commodity / raw material price and availability volatility
risks.note: The principal raw material is a variety of plastic polymers that are derivatives of crude oil, sourced primarily from the US, Middle East and Europe, with domestic prices generally in sync with international prices. Volatility in crude oil prices, rupee movement and the world demand-supply scenario affect the effective price and availability of polymers. In the last quarter of FY26 the escalation of the conflict in West Asia significantly affected raw material availability and pricing, impacting both margins and demand.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange exposure skewed to imports
risks.note: The Company operates internationally with a portion of business transacted in several currencies, and is exposed to FX risk through overseas sales and purchases from overseas suppliers. Management explicitly states that exports of the Company are significantly lower in comparison to its imports, so a depreciating rupee is a net cost headwind rather than a natural hedge; the exchange rate has changed substantially in recent years and may fluctuate substantially in future.

The Company's sole business segment is Plastic Films and all activities are incidental to this sole business segment, and it services both its domestic and export markets from India only - so there is no segment or manufacturing-geography diversification to absorb a shock to films demand, Indian input costs or India-specific trade measures.

risks.risk: Rising domestic competition in surface protection films
risks.note: Listed by management as a threat: a small number of domestic players have entered the surface protection films market, gradually increasing competitive intensity in what the Company describes as its core market.

risks.risk: End-demand dependence on the infrastructure and realty cycle
risks.note: Management states that demand for plastic in industrial applications, especially aluminium composite panel and surface protection film, will largely depend upon the revival of infrastructure projects as well as the realty sector, where consumption is large - making the Company's core volumes a derivative of a capex cycle it does not control.

risks.risk: Merger integration and restated comparatives following the Kunal Plastics amalgamation
risks.note: The auditor issued an Emphasis of Matter drawing attention to Note 40 on the Composite Scheme of Amalgamation of Kunal Plastics Private Limited into the Company from the retrospective appointed date of 1 April 2025 (NCLT order 14 May 2026, effective 28 May 2026), with the merger given effect as if it had occurred from the beginning of the preceding period per Appendix C to Ind AS 103. Opinion not modified, but FY26 and FY25 figures are on a merged basis, so reported history is not comparable to previously published standalone numbers, and the benefits of the enlarged entity are still to be delivered.

Named in the MD&A Risks and Concerns as the risk of financial loss if a customer or counter-party fails to meet contractual obligations; exposure is influenced mainly by the individual characteristics of each customer and the default risk of the customer's industry, managed through credit approvals, credit limits and continuous monitoring of creditworthiness.
